headline: Local Cafe Claims 'Quantum Entangled' Coffee Produces 47% Better Flavor
subheadline: Scientists remain skeptical, but customers report 'transcendent' experiences
summary: The Underground's new quantum brew method has attracted both devoted fans and harsh critics from the scientific community.
content:
The Underground, a beloved local venue known for its eclectic events and questionable acoustics, has unveiled what owner Marcus Chen calls "the most revolutionary coffee technology since the invention of the mug."

The process, which Chen describes as "quantum entanglement of flavor molecules," involves brewing two cups of coffee simultaneously in specially modified French presses. According to Chen, when one cup is consumed, the other cup "inherits the positive flavor intentions" of the drinker.

"It's simple physics," Chen explained while adjusting what appeared to be a modified microwave oven covered in Christmas lights. "When you observe coffee, you collapse its flavor waveform. We've found a way to collapse it in the most delicious direction."

Dr. Elena Martinez of the local university's physics department declined to comment on the scientific validity of the claims but was spotted purchasing a large quantum latte last Tuesday.

Regular customer Jake Morrison, 24, swears by the new method. "I've never felt more connected to my coffee," he said, staring intensely at his cup. "Sometimes I can almost taste what the coffee is feeling."

Pricing for the quantum coffee starts at $47 per cup, with discounts available for those who can prove they've read at least three Wikipedia articles about quantum mechanics.
author: Sandra Mitchell, Food & Science Correspondent
